title: Hollow and Ember
premise: Ansel Fairweather has spent her life in the Hollow, a valley where magic cannot follow, hiding the oath-bound gift of swordspeech that lets her hear and command the memories held in blades. When the crown's Ember Hunt sweeps toward the valley, she flees with a hunted fire-keeper named Wren and a disgraced hunt-captain, Sable, seeking the Door of Ash — the only way out of Vael, a country that officially no longer exists. Their journey forces Ansel to choose between erasing her gift to become safe and ordinary, or speaking the last dragon-fire awake and claiming an identity she was taught to bury. In the end she speaks the Door open not with power but with the found family who taught her that memory is something you carry together, and Vael — thought dead — breathes again.
about_author: Isandro Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who claims to have catalogued three thousand unsent letters before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who inherit things they never asked for.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. We meet Ansel in the Hollow, tending her late mentor's silent sword and hiding her gift from neighbors who prize forgetting. The crown's proclamation arrives: all gifted persons are to be taken for the Ember Hunt. Emotional beat: quiet dread as the safe numbness of her life cracks open.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Ashen Gate
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Wren, a fire-keeper with singed hands and a stolen ember-lantern, collapses at Ansel's door pursued by hunters. Ansel breaks her own rule and speaks to her mentor's sword for the first time in years — and it answers with her mentor's voice. Beat: reluctant courage; first bond formed.

chapters.title: What the Blade Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Fleeing through the valley's edge, Wren witnesses Ansel swordspeak for the first time and is awed rather than afraid. They learn the Hunt is led by Captain Sable, once oath-bound herself, now hunting her own kind. Beat: wonder shadowed by betrayal-to-come.

chapters.title: The Captain Who Burned Her Oath
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable corners them at a river ford but hesitates when Ansel speaks a sword Sable once carried — her own buried past returns. She lets them go, then defects, joining them under protest. Beat: shame meeting the possibility of forgiveness.

chapters.title: Roads Out of a Dead Country
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The trio crosses Vael's abandoned heartland: empty keeps, villages renamed by the crown, maps that deny the country exists. Wren teaches Ansel that fire remembers warmth, not just destruction. Beat: grief for a homeland becoming tenderness for companions.

chapters.title: The Ember Hunt Closes
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Hunters ambush them at a market built over old battlefields; animated weapons turn on their wielders when Ansel speaks. Wren is captured buying time. Sable must choose loyalty to the crown or to the family forming around her. Beat: fury and resolve.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A hedge-witch offers Ansel escape if she surrenders her gift — a painless hollowing of memory. Ansel nearly accepts, imagining safety, until the sword shows her a future where she forgets Wren entirely. Beat: the temptation of self-erasure confronted.

chapters.title: Door of Ash
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Rescued from the Hunt's camp by Sable's confession-turned-defiance, Wren leads them to the Door of Ash beneath a gutted volcano — but it only opens for spoken oaths, and the last dragon-fire is guttering. Beat: hope arriving hand-in-hand with impossibility.

chapters.title: The Last Oath
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The Hunt arrives at the threshold. Instead of fighting, Ansel speaks every blade present — including Sable's broken oath-sword — into one shared vow, feeding the dying dragon-fire with collective memory instead of her own alone. Beat: climax; identity claimed through connection, not sacrifice.

chapters.title: Hollow and Ember
chapters.summary: Rotating POVs. The Door opens; Vael re-enters the world's memory, and the Hunt dissolves as soldiers remember what they burned. Ansel keeps her gift, now shared rather than hidden, and chooses to stay with Wren and Sable. Beat: resolution — home rebuilt as people, not place.
